metadata.title: 2001 Case 38
metadata.original_presentation: A 51-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital because of paresthesias, ataxic gait, and hallucinations.

required.content: What symptoms did the patient experience initially?
required.response: The patient experienced tingling and numbness in all her fingers, weakness of her hands, and a burning sensation in her feet.

teaching_points.content: Paresthesias and weakness in extremities can indicate peripheral neuropathy.

required.content: What respiratory symptoms did the patient develop?
required.response: The patient developed 'asthmatic bronchitis' with a productive cough and mild hemoptysis.

teaching_points.content: Respiratory symptoms in smokers can be indicative of underlying malignancy.

required.content: What cognitive changes did the patient experience?
required.response: The patient had difficulty finding words and remembering the names of family members.

teaching_points.content: Cognitive changes can be associated with paraneoplastic syndromes.

required.content: What was the patient's smoking history?
required.response: The patient smoked three packs of cigarettes daily for 30 years.

teaching_points.content: Long-term smoking is a major risk factor for lung cancer.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) with exacerbation
supporting_evidence: history of smoking three packs daily for 30 years

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Multiple Sclerosis
refuting_evidence: age of onset is somewhat atypical
additional_information_needed: MRI of the brain and spinal cord

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Lung cancer with paraneoplastic syndrome
refuting_evidence: no direct evidence of a mass or cancer
additional_information_needed: biopsy if a mass is found

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chronic heavy metal poisoning (e.g., lead, mercury)

required.content: What were the findings on neurologic examination?
required.response: The patient was fully oriented, with impaired sensation of light touch and pinprick, absent sense of joint position and vibratory perception, mild dysmetria, extremely ataxic gait, and absent deep-tendon reflexes.

teaching_points.content: Neurologic examination can reveal signs of sensory neuropathy and ataxia.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Vitamin B12 deficiency
supporting_evidence: absent sense of joint position and vibratory perception

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) with hypoxemia
supporting_evidence: smoking three packs of cigarettes daily for 30 years
refuting_evidence: neurological symptoms are not typical for COPD

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Multiple sclerosis
refuting_evidence: smoking history and respiratory symptoms are not typical
additional_information_needed: MRI of the brain and spinal cord

required.content: What were the findings on chest radiograph and CT?
required.response: A hilar mass with mediastinal lymphadenopathy and blunting of the costophrenic angle on the right side.

teaching_points.content: Imaging can reveal masses indicative of malignancy.

required.content: What did the bronchoscopy and cytologic examination reveal?
required.response: Diffuse mucosal infiltration and thickening, with small mucosal nodules; fine-needle aspirate revealed undifferentiated small-cell carcinoma.

teaching_points.content: Bronchoscopy and cytology are key in diagnosing lung cancer.

required.content: What were the MRI findings of the brain and cervical spine?
required.response: Minimal prominence of ventricles, scattered foci of hyperintensity in white matter, straightening of cervical spine, and mild-to-moderate stenosis at C4–5 level.

teaching_points.content: MRI can identify structural changes and potential causes of neurologic symptoms.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Paraneoplastic Neuropathy
supporting_evidence: paresthesias, ataxic gait, absent deep-tendon reflexes, cognitive changes

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Small-Cell Lung Carcinoma with Metastasis
additional_information_needed: PET scan to assess for metastasis

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
supporting_evidence: smoking three packs daily for 30 years
refuting_evidence: no specific mention of airflow limitation or emphysema

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Vitamin B12 Deficiency
refuting_evidence: presence of small-cell lung carcinoma provides a more likely explanation

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Multiple Sclerosis
supporting_evidence: scattered foci of hyperintensity in white matter on MRI

required.content: What treatments were administered to the patient?
required.response: Cisplatin and etoposide, later substituted with carboplatin; radiation treatment; prednisone; comfort care.

teaching_points.content: Chemotherapy and radiation are standard treatments for small-cell lung cancer.

final_diagnosis.name: Paraneoplastic syndrome associated with small-cell lung cancer
supporting_evidence: Neurologic symptoms consistent with paraneoplastic syndrome
